description: A genuinely clean California offer letter for a software engineer, with nothing that qualifies under any of the four v1 clause types, so the correct output is a coverage receipt.
governingLaw: This letter shall be governed by the laws of the State of California.
decoySentences: Your employment with the Company is at will, meaning that either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause and with or without notice.

The option will vest over four (4) years, with twenty-five percent (25%) vesting on the first anniversary of your vesting commencement date and the remainder vesting in equal monthly installments over the following thirty-six (36) months, in each case subject to your continued service.

Once an option share has vested it remains vested, and the Company has no right to repurchase, cancel, or claw back any vested share or any vested portion of your equity on termination of your employment.

During and after your employment, you agree to hold in confidence and not to disclose the Company's Confidential Information, meaning non-public technical, product, customer, and financial information of the Company that is disclosed to you or developed by you in the course of your work.

Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of your own, that you lawfully knew before the Company disclosed it to you, or that you lawfully obtain from a third party without a duty of confidence.

You assign to the Company only those inventions and works of authorship that you create within the scope of your employment, using Company time, equipment, or Confidential Information, and that relate to the business of the Company.

This Section 5 does not apply to any invention that you develop entirely on your own time without using the Company's equipment, supplies, facilities, or Confidential Information, except for inventions that relate to the Company's business or that result from work performed by you for the Company.
You may list on the attached Schedule A any invention made before your employment that you wish to exclude from Section 5.1, and any invention so listed is excluded.
You are free to work on personal projects and open source software outside of working hours, and the Company makes no claim to that work where Section 5.1 does not apply to it.
